Rows\n// outside of a partial panel are padded with the identity.\n__global__ void potf2Kernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int J, const int nb,\n                            int* __restrict__ info) {\n    const unsigned mask = 0xffffffffu;\n    const int r = threadIdx.x;  // row within the block\n\n    double reg[NB];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int c = 0; c < NB; ++c) {\n        reg[c] = (r < nb && c < nb && c <= r) ? Rows\n// outside of a partial panel are padded with the identity.\n__global__ void potf2Kernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int J, const int nb,\n                            int* __restrict__ info) {\n    const unsigned mask = 0xffffffffu;\n    const int r = threadIdx.x;  // row within the block\n\n    double reg[NB];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int c = 0; c < NB; ++c) {\n        reg[c] = (r < nb && c < nb && c <= r) ? A[(size_t)(J + r) * n + (J + c)] : 0.0;\n    }\n    if (t < NB) {\n        rinv[t] = 1.0 / A[(size_t)(J + t) * n + (J + t)];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    const int i = J + NB + blockIdx.x * TRSM_T + t;\n    if (i >= n) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    double* __restrict__ row = A + (size_t)i * n + J;\n    double reg[NB];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int c = 0; c < NB; ++c) {\n        reg[c] = row[c];\n    }\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int j = 0; j < NB; ++j) {\n        double sum = 0.0;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n            sum += reg[k] * Ls[j][k];\n        }\n        reg[j] = (reg[j] - sum) * rinv[j];\n    }\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int c = 0; c < NB; ++c) {\n        row[c] = reg[c];\n    }\n}\n\n// Symmetric rank-NB update of the trailing submatrix: A -= L21 * L21^T.\n__global__ void syrkKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int J, const int base) {\n    const int bi = blockIdx.y;\n    const int bj = blockIdx.x;\n    if (bi < bj) {\n        return;  // strictly upper triangular tile, not referenced\n    }\n\n    __shared__ double As[TILE][NB + 1];\n    __shared__ double Bs[TILE][NB + 1];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int row0 = base + bi * TILE;\n    const int col0 = base + bj * TILE;\n\n    for (int r = ty; r < TILE; r += blockDim.y) {\n        const int gr = row0 + r;\n        const int gc = col0 + r;\n        As[r][tx] = (gr < n) ? A[(size_t)gr * n + J + tx] : 0.0;\n        Bs[r][tx] = (gc < n) ? A[(size_t)gc * n + J + tx] : 0.0;\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    double acc[RPT] = {0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0};\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int k = 0; k < NB; ++k) {\n        const double b = Bs[tx][k];\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int r = 0; r < RPT; ++r) {\n            acc[r] += As[ty + r * 8][k] * b;\n        }\n    }\n\n    const int j = col0 + tx;\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < RPT; ++r) {\n        const int i = row0 + ty + r * 8;\n        if (i < n && j <= i) {\n            A[(size_t)i * n + j] -= acc[r];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Zero the strictly upper triangular part of the rows [J, J + nb), which are\n// final once the diagonal block of the panel has been factored.\n__global__ void zeroUpperRowsKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int J,\n                                    const int nb) {\n    const int j = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const int r = blockIdx.y;\n    const int i = J + r;\n    if (r < nb && j < n && j > i) {\n        A[(size_t)i * n + j] = 0.0;\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Auxiliary kernels (matrix generation / validation)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// C = X * Y^T for row-major n x n matrices.\n__global__ void gemmNTKernel(const double* __restrict__ X, const double* __restrict__ Y,\n                             double* __restrict__ C, const int n) {\n    __shared__ double As[TILE][TILE + 1];\n    __shared__ double Bs[TILE][TILE + 1];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int row0 = blockIdx.y * TILE;\n    const int col0 = blockIdx.x * TILE;\n\n    double acc[RPT] = {0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0};\n\n    for (int kt = 0; kt < n; kt += TILE) {\n        const int k = kt + tx;\n        for (int r = ty; r < TILE; r += blockDim.y) {\n            const int gr = row0 + r;\n            const int gc = col0 + r;\n            As[r][tx] = (gr < n && k < n) ? r < RPT; ++r) {\n                acc[r] += As[ty + r * 8][kk] * b;\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    const int j = col0 + tx;\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < RPT; ++r) {\n        const int i = row0 + ty + r * 8;\n        if (i < n && j < n) {\n            C[(size_t)i * n + j] = acc[r];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n__global__ void addDiagonalKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const double value) {\n    const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i < n) {\n        A[(size_t)i * n + i] += value;\n    }\n}\n\n// Reduce max absolute / relative error between the reconstruction and the original.\n__global__ void errorKernel(const double* __restrict__ R, const double* __restrict__ Aorig,\n                            const idx += (size_t)gridDim.x * blockDim.x) {\n        const double error = fabs(R[idx] - Aorig[idx]);\n        maxAbs = fmax(maxAbs, error);\n        maxRel = fmax(maxRel, error / (fabs(Aorig[idx]) + 1e-10));\n    }\n\n    for (int offset = warpSize / 2; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {\n        maxAbs = fmax(maxAbs, __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, maxAbs, offset));\n        maxRel = fmax(maxRel, atomicMax(&out[0], (unsigned long long)__double_as_longlong(maxAbs));\n        atomicMax(&out[1], (unsigned long long)__double_as_longlong(maxRel));\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n Summary:\n\n## What changed\n\n**`cholesky/cholesky.cpp`** — same file, now compiled as CUDA:\n\n- **`choleskyDecomposition`** is a blocked right-looking factorization running entirely on the GPU, in panels of NB=32 columns:\n  - `potf2Kernel` — factors the 32×32 diagonal block with a *single warp*, one row per lane, exchanging rows via `__shfl_sync` (no barriers on this latency-critical path); pads partial panels with the identity.\n  - `trsmKernel` — triangular solve for all rows below the panel, fully unrolled with the row held in registers and the diagonal reciprocals precomputed in shared memory.\n  - `syrkKernel` — the bulk rank-32 trailing update, 32×32 shared-memory tiles, 4 outputs/thread; blocks strictly above the diagonal exit immediately.\n  - Finished panel rows are zeroed above the diagonal and streamed back to the host on a second stream (event-ordered) so the D2H transfer overlaps the trailing update; the host buffer is page-locked with `cudaHostRegister`.\n  - Non-positive-definite detection is kept via a device flag (`atomicMin` of the failing index), producing the same message and return value.\n- **Matrix generation and validation** also run on the GPU (shared tiled `gemmNTKernel` plus a `fmax`/`atomicMax` error reduction), so the untimed parts no longer take a minute at n=4096.\n\n**`cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`** — enables the CUDA language, compiles `cholesky.cpp` as CUDA (`native` architecture), keeps `-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra` for host code. Executable name unchanged, no new dependencies.\n\n## Results (decomposition time, vs. the original sequential build)\n\n| n | CPU | CUDA | speedup | GFLOPS |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 29 ms | 2 ms | 14× | 22 |\n| 1024 | 251 ms | 7 ms | 36× | 51 |\n| 2048 | 2124 ms | 15 ms | 142× | 191 |\n| 4096 | 17861 ms | 59 ms | 303× | 388 |\n| 8192 | ~143 s (extrap.) | 371 ms | ~385× | 494 |\n\n494 GFLOPS is ~89% of the RTX 3090's FP64 peak (~556 GFLOPS); the remaining time at n=4096 is ~10 ms of unavoidable H2D transfer plus ~7 ms of panel factorization.\n\n## Correctness\n\n`-v` validation passes for every size tested (1, 2, 31, 32, 33, 63, 100, 255, 257, 512, 1000, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192), and `-n 0` output matches the original byte-for-byte. The `-r` result blocks match the sequential reference to 1–2 ulp — the blocked algorithm sums the dot products in a different order, so the FNV hash of the doubles differs; `Sum`/`Min`/`Max`/samples agree to ~1e-15 relative and the reconstruction error stays ~1e-12 absolute.\n\nTwo things I deliberately did not do: I kept the host↔device transfer inside the timed region rather than caching the device matrix produced by the generator, and I left this single-GPU.
